tools.description: Lists the keys in the person's EnvCloak vault by name (slug), with each one's provider and whether it is a test or live key. Never returns a value. With project_dir, also shows which variables that project's envcloak.toml binds to which keys, and whether each binding resolves. Use run_with_secrets to run a command with them; use add_reference to bind one to a variable.

project_dir.description: Absolute path of a project directory: its envcloak.toml (there or above) is read for its bindings.

tools.name: list_secrets
tools.title: List the keys EnvCloak holds

tools.description: Shows where a project stands with EnvCloak, metadata only: its envcloak.toml and whether each binding resolves, how many plaintext keys its .env files still hold, the requests this server's run_with_secrets calls left waiting for the person's approval, the grants for this agent, and which EnvCloak features are unavailable in this version. Never returns a value.

project_dir.description: Absolute path of the project directory.

tools.name: project_status
tools.title: Show a project's EnvCloak status

tools.description: Adds a binding to the project's envcloak.toml: the variable env_name will get the key the slug names when a command runs through EnvCloak. Takes names only, never a value; only keys of the secret class can be bound (find them with list_secrets). The binding is a request, not an approval: the next run that uses it asks the person.

env_name.description: The environment variable, such as OPENAI_API_KEY.

project_dir.description: Absolute path of the project directory; its envcloak.toml (there or above) is edited.

slug.description: The key's slug as list_secrets shows it, optionally with #<field>.

tools.name: add_reference
tools.title: Bind a variable to a key in envcloak.toml

tools.description: Runs a command with the keys the project's envcloak.toml names in its environment, through `envcloak run`: the same approval, policy and redaction as running `envcloak run -- <argv>` in a shell. In the command's output each key, and its common encodings, are masked; output the command transforms (part of a key, a re-encoding, compression or encryption) is not. A command needs the person's approval in EnvCloak, given from a terminal of their own; until then the result names the pending request, and the call can be made again once it is approved. The command runs outside this host's sandbox, and holds the injected keys in its environment and memory while it runs: what it does with them (files, network, its own child processes) is up to the command. argv runs without a shell; output is cut to its first and last 64 KiB per stream. A status of execution_unknown means the command may have run: check before running it again.

argv.description: The command and its arguments, run without a shell. Never put a key here.

project_dir.description: Absolute path of the project directory: the command runs there, and its envcloak.toml (there or above) names the keys.

tools.name: run_with_secrets
tools.title: Run a command with the project's keys

tools.description: Use when a key the project needs is not in EnvCloak (list_secrets does not show it). Takes the provider's name only, never a key, and returns what to ask the person: to run `envcloak add <provider>` in a terminal of their own and enter the key at its hidden prompt. Never ask the person to paste a key into this conversation. In this version EnvCloak has no app to paste into.

provider.description: The provider's name in EnvCloak's registry, such as openai, stripe or github.

tools.name: request_new_secret
tools.title: Ask the person to add a key

tools.description: Signs in to a registered development target with stored credentials after the person approves in EnvCloak, and delivers the resulting session to EnvCloak's hosted browser context. The resulting session acts as that account on the target's origins for the session's lifetime. Cancelling a tool call only stops waiting for an answer; call cancel_sign_in to end the operation itself. Takes the target name, optional role, and an idempotency operation_key (never echoed or logged), never a credential value, URL, script, callback, or DevTools address, and never returns a password, TOTP code, cookie, or storage token.

operation_key.description: Caller-chosen idempotency key (`1..=128` characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`). Never echoed or logged.

project_dir.description: Optional absolute path of the project directory whose envcloak.toml scopes the sign-in request.

role.description: Optional role name on the target (`1..=64` characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`). Never a URL, script, callback, or DevTools address.

target.description: Name of the registered sign-in target (`1..=128` characters of `[a-z0-9._-/]` starting and ending with `[a-z0-9]`, e.g. `acme/local`). Never a URL, script, callback, or DevTools address.

tools.name: request_sign_in
tools.title: Sign in to a development target

tools.description: Checks the status of a sign-in operation started with request_sign_in (which signs in with stored credentials after the person approves in EnvCloak, so the resulting session acts as that account). Cancelling a tool call only stops waiting for an answer; call cancel_sign_in to end the operation itself, or end_sign_in_session to close an active session. Never returns a credential value, cookie, or storage token.

request.description: The 32-character lowercase hex request identifier returned by request_sign_in.

tools.name: sign_in_status
tools.title: Check a sign-in operation's status

tools.description: Ends a sign-in operation started with request_sign_in (which signs in with stored credentials after the person approves in EnvCloak, producing a session that acts as that account). Cancelling a request_sign_in or sign_in_status tool call only stops waiting for an answer; cancel_sign_in ends the operation itself, stops any in-flight sign-in worker, and tears down any browser context it opened.

request.description: The 32-character lowercase hex request identifier returned by request_sign_in.

tools.name: cancel_sign_in
tools.title: Cancel a sign-in operation

tools.description: Ends an active browser session delivered by request_sign_in (which signed in with stored credentials after the person approved in EnvCloak, so the session acts as that account). Cancelling a tool call only stops waiting while cancel_sign_in ends a pending or running operation; end_sign_in_session closes the delivered browser context, runs configured server-side revocation, and confirms local cleanup.

session.description: The delivered session handle (`ctx-...`) or 32-character lowercase hex request identifier to end.

tools.name: end_sign_in_session
tools.title: End a delivered sign-in session
